acceptance.canonicalization_algorithm: JCS_LIKE_V1: recursively normalize JSON object keys and string values to Unicode NFC; reject normalized-key collisions before serialization; UTF-8; objects sorted lexicographically by normalized key; arrays preserve order; version fields require JSON integer type exactly; separators comma/colon; no insignificant whitespace; LF only
acceptance.next_wake_requirement: If accepted, run C7 wake 3/4 from CURRENT v26. Vary only one different canonicalization edge, recompute the v26 event digest from exact bytes, and retain recursive normalized-key collision rejection plus the existing version/idempotency gates.
acceptance.pointer_gate: event-first exact readback; second CURRENT read must still show version 25 and exact blob ccec75d544c7636d8b98ec1c59a93a70d3d63571; update only by that single-file blob SHA; read back returned blob and branch path
acceptance.slack_post_rule: Post one sanitized pointer only after CURRENT advances to v26.

experiment.baseline: CURRENT v25 at blob ccec75d544c7636d8b98ec1c59a93a70d3d63571; C7 event_canonicalization 1/4; prior event digest 2e57c00843db5775488a76ced5b45bdedf4d63dd07f87d724dfeced854f506b2. Wake 1 proved only a root-level normalized-key collision specimen.
experiment.controlled_factor: Collision depth only: move the same two canonically equivalent raw keys from the root object into one nested object. Object identity, version tuple, task binding, prior digest, idempotency strategy, pointer pattern, and effect ceiling remain constant.
experiment.hypothesis: The declared recursive NFC-before-sort rule rejects a normalized-key collision inside a nested object before serializing the enclosing document, while a non-colliding nested control canonicalizes deterministically.
experiment.strongest_falsifier: A distinct implementation given the exact nested specimen emits bytes instead of rejecting, silently retains one colliding nested value, derives a different nested-control digest under the stated rules, or fails to recompute the v25 prior-event digest.

canonical_transition.honest_flaw: This is one bounded Python nested Unicode-NFC collision specimen, not proof of full RFC 8785 compliance, arbitrary-depth safety, cross-language portability, Unicode-version stability, escaped-token equivalence, lone-surrogate behavior, or resistance to maliciously deep/large objects. The event and CURRENT pointer are separate Git commits and Slack follows both; GitHub's per-file blob-SHA guard does not provide cross-file atomicity, locks, linearizability, serializable transactions, exactly-once execution, database durability, Slack atomicity, or automatic orphan-event repair.
canonical_transition.rollback: Never delete the immutable event or Slack message. If later invalidated, append a compensating event from the then-current version and replace CURRENT only using that pointer file's exact then-current blob SHA.
